items.title: Henry Johnson interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 30, 1995
items.q: I was working with a big band that worked all of the society functions, Morris Allen, who still has a big band now today

ctx.x: Now I want to ask you something about a guitar trio. That is, that really takes some kind of player, because you think of a trio you think of a keyboard player, because he can play chords with his left hand and he can solo with his right hand. So he can kind of comp behind himself. But with you just, what’d you have just bass and drums? That’s a lot of work.

I was too young to know it was a lot of work. I mean you know when I started doing the songs of the day at that time, was “Bet You By Golly Wow” and all that kind of stuff, I didn’t know that was a lot of work. So what I did was I hired a singer, a female singer, who, she sang half of the show and I played the other half. And it was odd because I © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

never missed a piano player at that time. But later on when I started, after that I was working with a big band that worked all of the society functions, Morris Allen, who still has a big band now today, and through that I started really getting, I always liked big band music, and when I was in Memphis I also played clarinet. Because I wanted to play trumpet but they didn’t have a trumpet then so the only thing they had left was the clarinet so I played the clarinet so I could be in the band, in the junior high…
